title: Why Power Corrupts
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece explains the psychological mechanics by which accumulating leadership power can erode a person's ethics over time. It traces a progression: as leaders gain the authority to reward and punish, that power stimulates feelings of superiority and entitlement, which in turn erodes the sense of accountability to others. Reduced accountability opens the door to unearned privileges, and the desire for more of those privileges becomes self-reinforcing. The piece names weak character as the variable that determines whether this pressure tips into genuinely unethical behavior, and offers a countermeasure: leaders who deliberately share opportunities, rewards, and experiences with their teams resist the corrosive pull of accumulated power.
points: The mechanism of corruption is traced as a chain: accumulated power breeds superiority and entitlement, which erodes felt accountability, which opens the door to unearned privilege.
The piece names "weak character" as the deciding factor in whether a leader crosses the line from enjoying legitimate perks into unethical self-dealing.
The recommended countermeasure is deliberately sharing rewards, access, and experiences with the team rather than accumulating them personally.
The closing line reframes power as something that, like affection, "must be shared to be really enjoyed" — reframing generosity as self-interest well understood.
quotes: Leaders who overstep and misuse their power for personal benefit never recover.
The more power they accumulate over time, the more this influence stimulates feelings of superiority, entitlement, and inflated self-worth.
The more powerful a leader becomes, the more they come to believe they are less accountable for their actions.

To maintain the power that infuses them with such an inflated self-importance, those weak in character will sometimes cross a line and engage in selfish acts that can become unethical or unscrupulous.
Great leaders spread the wealth. They refuse to accumulate the trappings of success and push whatever comes their way to others.
For the best leaders, power is like affection. It must be shared to be really enjoyed.
